record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Mixed-smoothness logarithmic loss under iid sampling
record.original_question: For functions with mixed smoothness on the d-torus, specifically the space H_d^{k,mix}(T^d), independent uniformly distributed sample points are known to be optimal for the Monte Carlo error and optimal up to a logarithmic factor for the uniform error, which also yields logarithmic-factor optimality for integration. Can that logarithmic loss be removed for uniformly distributed samples, as happens in the isotropic-smoothness setting?

evidence.quote: There are recent results in this direction for the special case of L2-approximation on the Hilbert space Hk,mix(Td) of functions with mixed smoothness k on the d-torus. Namely, it is known that independent and uniformly distributed sampling points are optimal with respect to the Monte Carlo error [54] and optimal up to a logarithmic factor with respect to the uniform error [20, 61, 113].

This also implies that they are optimal up to logarithmic factors for the problem of integration on Hk,mix(Td) with respect to both error criteria. We do not know whether the logarithmic loss can be avoided with uniformly distributed samples, as it is the case with isotropic smoothness. This is another Open Problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^d = \mathbb{R}^d / \mathbb{Z}^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional torus, equipped with the normalized Lebesgue measure. For an integer $k \ge 1$, let $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ denote the Hilbert space of functions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ with dominating mixed smoothness $k$, namely the space of $f \in L_2(\mathbb{T}^d)$ whose Fourier coefficients $\hat f(\mathbf{m})$, $\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, satisfy
$$\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}^2 \;=\; \sum_{\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{Z}^d} \Big(\prod_{j=1}^d (1+|m_j|)^{2k}\Big)\, |\hat f(\mathbf{m})|^2 \;<\; \infty.$$

Consider the integration problem $I(f) = \int_{\mathbb{T}^d} f(x)\,dx$ and randomized linear quadrature rules $Q_n(f) = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(X_i)$ where the nodes $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are required to be independent and uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{T}^d$ (the coefficients $a_i$ may depend on the nodes). Define the worst-case error under iid uniform sampling by
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;=\; \inf_{a_1,\dots,a_n} \;\sup_{\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}\le 1} \;\mathbb{E}\,\big|I(f)-Q_n(f)\big|,$$
and let $e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$ denote the corresponding optimal worst-case error over all randomized algorithms using $n$ function evaluations at arbitrary (possibly adaptive) sample points.

It is known that iid uniform sampling is optimal for $L_2$-approximation in $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ with respect to the Monte Carlo (mean-square) error, and optimal up to a logarithmic factor with respect to the uniform error, which yields
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;\le\; C(d,k)\,(\log n)^{\alpha(d,k)}\, e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$$
for some exponent $\alpha(d,k)>0$.

Question: Can the logarithmic factor be removed? More precisely, does there exist a constant $C=C(d,k)$ such that
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;\le\; C\, e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$$
for all $n\ge 2$, as is known in the isotropic-smoothness setting?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in the literature on optimal numerical integration for mixed-smoothness function spaces. Recent surveys and papers on iid sampling recovery and integration on $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ confirm that, while iid uniform points are known to be optimal up to logarithmic factors, removing the logarithmic loss for integration in this setting remains unresolved. A related result in the isotropic Sobolev case shows the logarithmic factor can be avoided except for $p=q=\infty$, but the mixed-smoothness analogue is still not established.

status_evidence.title: Recovery of Sobolev functions restricted to iid sampling
status_evidence.snippet: Studies optimal randomized algorithms versus iid uniform sampling for Sobolev spaces, showing matching rates except in the p=q=∞ case where a logarithmic loss appears.
status_evidence.claim: In the isotropic-smoothness case the logarithmic loss can typically be removed, motivating the mixed-smoothness question.

status_evidence.title: Sparse-grid sampling recovery and numerical integration of functions having mixed smoothness
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys current results on sampling recovery and integration for $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$, with logarithmic gaps still present in several settings.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal rates for integration on mixed-smoothness spaces from iid samples are known only up to logarithmic factors.
